claims.claim: **Opportunistic education on oral hygiene and dental access** can prevent caries and odontogenic infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Over 40% of Australian children have caries**, which can start as soon as teeth erupt. Early childhood caries is concentrated on the upper front teeth, in breast- and bottle-fed children who keep feeding or comfort-sucking at night.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wipe infants' teeth and gums; from over 12 months, brush twice daily with a smear of paediatric fluoridated toothpaste**, done or supervised by a parent. **Annual dental review.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Persistent thumb-sucking or dummy use after 3 years: dental consultation and cessation counselling.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about** cardiac conditions that may need endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures, and medicines that reduce saliva (e.g. antihistamines, anticonvulsants, antidepressants) or cause gum hypertrophy (e.g. phenytoin).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **'Lift the lip'** to examine the upper front teeth and gums; look for white or brown spots or lines at the gum line that don't brush off.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Abscess signs:** tender gingival swelling or erythema, a draining gingival sinus, facial cellulitis over the tooth, submandibular or periorbital areas, trismus. **There may be no fever or systemic symptoms.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **An established abscess usually needs root canal therapy or extraction.** Definitive treatment, i.e. extraction, is still needed after pain and infection are treated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give antibiotics for spreading infection, systemic signs, or when definitive dental treatment will be delayed more than 24 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Localised infection:** e.g. **oral amoxicillin 25 mg/kg (max 500 mg) three times a day.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Spreading, no systemic features:** e.g. **amoxicillin/clavulanate 22.5/3.2 mg/kg (max 875/125 mg) orally bd for 5 days.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Spreading infection with severe or systemic features:** e.g. **IV amoxicillin/clavulanate 6-hourly.** The page's dose figure is ambiguous and is not restated here — see Unresolved.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow local susceptibility patterns.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bleeding after treatment** comes from a disturbed clot or a bleeding disorder. **Assess haemodynamic status**, rinse the mouth with cold water, and **bite on gauze for 30 minutes**; if bleeding continues, consider tranexamic-acid-soaked gauze. Treat any bleeding disorder; surgical dressing or sutures may be needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe bleeding:** firm pressure, IV access, IV fluids, FBE, coagulation studies, cross-match; **discuss with haematology and maxillofacial surgery.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Usually no intervention.** Extract if very loose, an inhalation risk, interfering with breastfeeding, or ulcerating the tongue, frenulum or lip.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the specialist paediatric dental team** for an abscess with severe or systemic features needing admission, or a child whose medical, developmental or behavioural needs call for specialist dental, anaesthetic or haematology input.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** if specialist dental or maxillofacial care is not available locally.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** suitable for oral therapy, with cellulitis improving and extraction planned or done.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Public dental access** is set by each state; some children qualify for the Child Dental Benefits Schedule.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23
